hypothesis: A caller-owned immutable question-to-fact registry catches question substitution and registered evidence misassociation, while same-ID wrong-answer and negation controls demonstrate that such binding is not semantic verification.
expected_boundaries: Literal question identity and exact caller-required fact IDs are mechanical requirements, not semantic equivalence.
A legitimate paraphrase is refused under literal policy; report separately, not zero semantic false rejection.
Answer text with correct IDs/tokens can remain false; binding result must never be named technical acceptance.
No inference reruns, source execution, production modifications or original output repair.
